questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Good university within the culture and art department with a large variety of different courses. But in general I choose University of Edinburgh because I wanted to explore and live in Scotland because of my Scottish herritage.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found the CAHSS office within University of Edinburgh quite helpful, and they were quick answering questions and doubts upon arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I only received assistance through mail correspondance with CAHSS.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Don't know, I lived off campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That it is far more local to live off campus, so if future exchange students want to experience a more calm, local vibe of Edinburgh, they should try to find a place a bit away from city center campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: No housing for exchange students going abroad for six months! Only available for students taking a full academic year.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There was a thorough video guide on University of Edinburghs website showing you have to register at the university. Still, it was a bit confusing. A lot of steps were necessary in order to fully matriculate, having to be done on different platforms.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Video guide and CAHSS office per mail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was quite lucky and in the end ended up with courses that I had wished for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't worry! You will be registered one way or another.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had two third year level courses and one first year level courses. The difference was quite big, but it was out of interest that I have chosen all of them. In general I think the level of courses at University of Edinburgh is quite high and the teachers are talented.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I found the style of teaching and the expectations of the written papers more conservative and restricted as opposed to UCPH. It was more a question of saying or writing what you know instead of analysing and discussing what might be.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Sinners, Saints and Seers: Scottish, Irish and English Art from 600-900
Sustainable Sculpture Practice
Films on Film

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend going for courses at ECA (Edinburgh College of Art). It is a beautiful building with lots of interesting courses within art, art history and architecture.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: All the events and trips the university arrange! Some are good, but it's not for free.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Going out having a beer or a coffee were more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: University of Edinburgh has a lot of societies, whether you are into theatre, sports, music, beer, pole dancing etc. It does cost something to be a member of these societies which is also an extra cost one should have in mind.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Going to The Jazz bar, where the Edinburgh Jazz Society (students) play (and it's free!). In general go to pubs and hear folk music.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The Highlands, Glasgow, Loch Lomond.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it quite easy. I'm part Scottish, so for me it was like coming home, even though I haven't lived in Scotland before.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go outside academic/university activities! Most of the students are international students like yourself, so if one wants to talk to local people, go to Leith or somewhere outside campus.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The open-hearted, open-minded, straight forward, kind and funny Scottish people!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Very few actual Scotts attend University of Edinburgh (so bear this in mind, you will meet mostly international students), the country and culture is absolutely beautiful, stay away from Buckfast.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Edinburgh is a good size for being on exchange for only half a year, and the nature surrounding it makes a magical city.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To get to live in Scotland.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and having the energy to do all the stuff you wanted to do. Going on exchange can be quite challenging in itself; a new educational system to learn, new expectations, new courses, new city and new surroundings.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
